# iliad-020 (3.369–461) — new renderings

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς φάτο, τῇ δ’ ἄρα θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ὄρινε (3.395; same Greek as odyssey-083, line 150, whose English is "So he spoke, and the heart in her breast he stirred." / "So he spoke, and he stirred the heart in her breast.") | "So she spoke, and the heart in her breast she stirred." | "So she spoke, and she stirred the heart in her breast." | "So he spoke…" (the Odyssey’s English, said there of a man; here the speaker is Aphrodite, so only the pronouns change); the note says the line is shared with the Odyssey; the Odyssey table’s ὣς φάτο row for a female speaker says the pronoun alone tracks the speaker’s sex, and its row for this line (17.150) is the English reused |
| ἱπποδάσεια (κόρυθος ἱπποδασείης, 3.369) | "horse-haired" | "thick with horsehair" | "plumed" alone, "crested" (reserved for λόφος), "horse-tailed" (the Odyssey’s ἵππουρις), "horsehair-thick" (the first draft, changed at review); the Odyssey table’s κυνέας ἱπποδασείας "horse-haired" / "thick with horsehair" (22.111), unchanged; ἵππος + δασύς "thick, shaggy" |
| πολύκεστος (ἱμὰς πολύκεστος, 3.371; meaning uncertain) | "much-embroidered" | "richly embroidered" (+ note: sense not certain) | "many-stitched", "richly decorated" (each decides the sense); κεστός is "stitched" |
| ἶφι κταμένοιο (βοὸς ἶφι κταμένοιο, 3.375) | "slain with force" | "killed by force" | "slain by a mighty blow", "slain outright"; ἶφι keeps the table’s "with force / powerfully" (ἶφι ἀνάσσεις, ἶφι μάχεσθαι); κτάμενος is the epic aorist participle of κτείνω "kill" |
| ἠέρι πολλῇ (3.381) | "thick mist" | "thick mist" | "much mist", "deep mist", "a cloud"; ἀήρ in Homer is mist, as in the table’s κεκαλυμμέναι ἠέρι καὶ νεφέλῃ |
| εὐώδης · κηώεις (θαλάμῳ εὐώδεϊ κηώεντι, 3.382) | "sweet-smelling" · "fragrant" | "sweet-smelling" · "fragrant" | "fragrant … fragrant" (the two Greek words stay apart in one line); εὐώδης keeps the shipped "sweet-smelling" (ἐυῶδες ἔλαιον, odyssey-008) and κηώεις the table’s "fragrant" |
| νεκταρέου ἑανοῦ (3.385) | "nectar-sweet robe" | "robe, sweet as nectar" (+ note: νεκτάρεος "like nectar", the usual explanation) | "nectared", "nectarous" (archaic), "fragrant" (kept for κηώεις); ἑανός is a fine robe |
| παλαιγενής (γρηῒ … παλαιγενέϊ, 3.386) | "of ancient birth" | "of great age" | "old-born", "ancient", "long-lived", "aged" (the table keeps "aged" for the plain παλαιή); the Odyssey table’s παλαιγενής (22.395) "of ancient birth" / "of great age", unchanged; the first draft had "aged" / "very old", changed at review |
| εἰροκόμος (3.387) | "wool-tender" | "wool-dresser" | "wool-worker", "weaver" (a different craft); εἶρος "wool" + κομέω "tend" |
| τῇ μιν ἐεισαμένη προσεφώνεε δῖ’ Ἀφροδίτη (3.389, whole-line speech introduction) | "Having made herself like to her, addressed heavenly Aphrodite:" | "Heavenly Aphrodite, making herself like her, spoke to her:" | "answered" (nothing has been said to her); follows the Odyssey table’s τῇ μιν ἐεισαμένη προσέφη γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (6.24), with προσεφώνεε "addressed" / "spoke to" as in the table’s προσεφώνεεν Ἶρος (18.25) |
| δινωτοῖσι λέχεσσι (3.391) | "round-wrought bedstead" | "bedstead worked in rounds" | "inlaid bed", "carved bed" (each decides how it is decorated), "couches" (reserved for εὐνή); δινωτός follows the shipped "round-wrought" / "worked in rounds" (odyssey-092); the plural is one bedstead, as in τρητοῖς … λεχέεσσιν |
| ἱμερόεις (στήθεά θ’ ἱμερόεντα, 3.397) | "full of longing" | "full of longing" | "lovely" (reserved for ἐρατεινός; the Odyssey table turns it down for ἱμερόεις), "desirable"; follows the Odyssey table’s ἱμερόεις γόος, χορὸν ἱμερόεντα and ἔπεα ἱμερόεντα "full of longing" (ἵμερος "longing" + -όεις); the first draft had "lovely", changed at review. The shipped "lovely song" of odyssey-004 and odyssey-090 (ἱμερόεσσαν ἀοιδήν) predates these rows and is not followed |
| ὄμματα μαρμαίροντα (3.397) | "sparkling eyes" | "sparkling eyes" | "flashing" (reserved for ἀστεροπητής), "shining" (φαεινός), "gleaming" (γλαυκῶπις); μαρμαίρω "flash, sparkle" |
| νικάω (νικήσας, 3.404; ἐνίκησεν, 3.439; the verb understood at 3.440) | "prevailed over" · "prevailed" · "(shall prevail over)" | "defeated" · "won" · "defeat" | "conquered", "overcame" (reserved for δάμνημι "subdue"); the table’s νικάω "prevail over, surpass" (2.370), here of a real contest |
| ἄγεσθαι (οἴκαδ’ ἄγεσθαι, 3.404) | "to take … home with him" | "to take … home with him" | "to lead home" (loses the middle); the middle is "for himself" |
| δολοφρονέουσα (3.405) | "with guile in your mind" | "with guile in your mind" | "scheming" and "plotting" (the Odyssey table turns them down: each drops φρήν "mind"), "with treacherous thoughts"; follows the Odyssey table’s δολοφρονέων "with guile in his mind" (18.51; odyssey-088, odyssey-104), person changed. The shipped odyssey-048 has "scheming with guile" for the same participle (10.339); it predates the row and is not followed; the first draft had followed it, changed at review |
| νεμεσσητὸν δέ κεν εἴη (3.410) | "it would be a thing to resent" | "that would be a thing to resent" | the Odyssey’s English (odyssey-110, line 489) with the closing mark removed; the table’s νεμεσσητόν "a thing to resent" |
| ἄχε’ ἄκριτα (3.412) | "griefs, unsorted" | "endless griefs" | "countless griefs", "confused sorrows"; ἄκριτος keeps "unsorted" in `l` (2.246) and takes its sense, "without end", in `i` (2.796); ἄχος "grief" |
| τὴν δὲ χολωσαμένη προσεφώνεε δῖ’ Ἀφροδίτη (3.413, whole-line speech introduction) | "And her, enraged, addressed heavenly Aphrodite:" | "Then heavenly Aphrodite, enraged, spoke to her:" | "furious", "angry" (reserved for χόλος); follows the Odyssey table’s τὸν δὲ χολωσάμενος προσεφώνεεν Ἶρος (18.25) |
| σχετλίη (vocative, 3.414) | "cruel one" | "cruel one" | "hard one", "headstrong", "unbending"; follows the table’s σχέτλιος "cruel one" |
| ἀπεχθήρω (3.415) | "hate" | "hate" (+ note: could be "make hateful") | "make hateful to" (decides the open sense), "come to hate"; ἀπεχθαίρω "hate" |
| ἔκπαγλα φιλέω (ἔκπαγλ’ ἐφίλησα, 3.415) | "terribly … loved" | "terribly … loved" | "madly", "fiercely" (each changes the degree); the table’s ἐκπάγλως "terribly" in both layers |
| ἔχθεα λυγρά (3.416) | "grievous hatreds" | "grievous hatreds" | "bitter enmities", "grievous enmity"; ἔχθος "hatred", λυγρός "grievous" |
| κακὸν οἶτον ὄληαι (3.417) | "perish by an evil fate" | "perish by an evil fate" | "die an evil death", "meet an evil doom" (the Odyssey’s `l` for οἶτον in odyssey-010); οἶτος "fate", as in odyssey-004 |
| ἀργῆτι (ἑανῷ ἀργῆτι φαεινῷ, 3.419) | "bright" | "bright" | "white", "shining" (reserved for φαεινός); ἀργής "bright, white", as in the Odyssey’s ἀργῆτι κεραυνῷ "bright thunderbolt" |
| κατασχομένη (3.419) | "covering herself" | "covering herself" | "veiling herself", "drawing her robe about her" (each adds a detail); κατέχω "hold down", middle "cover oneself" |
| λάθεν (πάσας δὲ Τρῳὰς λάθεν, 3.420) | "she escaped the notice of" | "escaped the notice of" | "she was unseen by", "none noticed her"; follows the Odyssey’s λάθεν "escaped notice" (odyssey-042, odyssey-058) |
| ἦρχε δὲ δαίμων (3.420; of Aphrodite) | "and led the divinity" | "and the divinity led the way" | "the goddess" (names her), "some power" (the Odyssey table’s δαίμων for one unnamed power acting on a man), "the spirit"; follows the Iliad’s δαίμονας ἄλλους "the other divinities" (1.222) |
| ἀμφίπολοι (3.422) | "handmaids" | "handmaids" | "attendants" (the Odyssey table’s word for ἀμφίπολοι; the Iliad has shipped "handmaids" at 3.143, which this part follows, and the Odyssey ships "handmaid" for ἀμφίπολος Σικελή), "servants" (reserved for δμῶες) |
| δίφρον (of a seat, 3.424) | "stool" | "stool" | "chair" (reserved for θρόνος), "seat" (reserved for κλισμός), "chariot" (the same word in 3.262 and 3.312; context tells them apart) |
| ὄσσε πάλιν κλίνασα (3.427) | "her eyes turning away" | "turning her eyes away" | "turning her eyes back", "lowering her eyes" (each decides why); ὄσσε "eyes" (a dual), πάλιν "back, away" |
| ἠνίπαπε μύθῳ (3.427) | "rebuked with a word" | "rebuked … in these words" | follows the Odyssey table’s ἠνίπαπε μύθῳ (20.17) "rebuked with a word" / "rebuked … in these words" |
| ὡς ὤφελες … ὀλέσθαι (3.428) | "would that you had perished" | "if only you had perished" | "you should have died" (a rebuke the Greek does not make); ὄφελες "would that", as in the table’s αἴθ’ ὄφελες |
| ὃς ἐμὸς πρότερος πόσις ἦεν (3.429) | "who was my former husband" | "who was my husband before you" | "my first husband"; πρότερος "former", as in the shipped "your former husband" (3.163) |
| εὔχομαι + infinitive (εὔχε’ … φέρτερος εἶναι, 3.430–431) | "were claiming … to be stronger" | "used to claim that you were stronger" | "boasted" (the Odyssey table turns it down for "claimed"), "prayed"; the table’s εὔχεται εἶναι (2.82) "claims to be" |
| βίη (σῇ τε βίῃ, 3.431) | "might" | "might" | "strength" (reserved for κράτος), "force" (reserved for ἶφι); follows βίη Ἡρακληείη "the might of Heracles" (2.658) |
| ἐναντίον (3.433) | "opposite him" | "to face you" | "face to face" (reserved for ἀντίον), "head-on"; ἐναντίον "opposite, in person" |
| ἀντίβιον πόλεμον πολεμίζειν (3.435) | "an opposing war to wage" | "to wage open war" | "a war of opposition", "to fight a hostile war"; ἀντίβιος keeps "opposing" (ἀντιβίοισι ἐπέεσσιν "words of opposition", 1.304), and the noun and the verb of one root are both shown in `l`, as in the table’s ἄπρηκτον πόλεμον πολεμίζειν |
| ἀφραδέως (3.436) | "senselessly" | "senselessly" | "rashly", "foolishly" (reserved for νήπιος); ἀφραδής "senseless" in the Odyssey table |
| κέλομαι (παύεσθαι κέλομαι, 3.434) | "urge" | "urge" | "bid", "order" (a command, which is not what she means); the table’s κέλομαι "bid / order", "urge" for advice |
| τὴν δὲ Πάρις μύθοισιν ἀμειβόμενος προσέειπε (3.437, whole-line speech introduction) | "And her Paris with words, answering, addressed:" | "Paris answered her and spoke in these words:" | "replied" alone, "Paris answered with words" (drops προσέειπε); follows the Odyssey table’s ἐξαῦτις μύθοισιν ἀμειβόμενος προσέειπε (24.350) |
| γύναι (vocative, Paris to Helen, 3.438) | "wife" | "wife" | "woman" (the plain address, as to a stranger, 3.204), "lady", "dear"; follows the Odyssey table’s γύναι "wife" for a husband to a wife (8.424) |
| θυμὸν ἔνιπτε (3.438) | "rebuke my heart" | "rebuke me to the heart" | "scold", "chide"; ἐνίπτω keeps "rebuke" (the Odyssey table), θυμός "heart" |
| ἀλλ’ ἄγε δὴ φιλότητι τραπείομεν εὐνηθέντε (3.441) | "But come now, to love let us turn, having lain down, we two" | "But come, let us turn to love, lying down together" | follows the shipped Odyssey line δεῦρο, φίλη, λέκτρονδε τραπείομεν εὐνηθέντες (odyssey-036) "let us turn" / "lying down"; "make love" (decides the sense of φιλότητι) |
| ἔρως · ἵμερος (3.442, 3.446) | "desire" · "longing" | "desire" · "longing" | "love" (reserved for φιλότης), "passion"; ἔραμαι "I desire" keeps the family of ἔρως, and ἵμερος is "longing" (3.139) |
| ἀμφικαλύπτω φρένας (3.442) | "enfolded my wits" | "enfolded my wits" | "covered my mind", "overwhelmed my senses"; follows the table’s ἀμφικαλύπτει αἰδῶ "enfold your shame" |
| ἐμίγην φιλότητι καὶ εὐνῇ (3.445) | "I was mingled in love and in bed" | "I lay with you in love" | follows the Odyssey table’s μίγη φιλότητι καὶ εὐνῇ (5.126) "was mingled in love and in bed" / "lay in love with …" |
| τρητοῖσι λεχέεσσιν (3.448) | "bored bedstead" | "corded bedstead" | follows the shipped τρητοῖς ἐν λεχέεσσιν (Odyssey 3.399) "a bored bedstead" / "a corded bedstead" |
| θηρὶ ἐοικώς (3.449) | "like a wild beast" | "like a wild beast" | "like a beast", "like a lion" (names what the Greek does not); θήρ "wild beast" |
| κλειτῶν ἐπικούρων (3.451) | "famous allies" | "famous allies" | "glorious allies", "renowned"; κλειτός = κλυτός "famous", ἐπίκουρος "ally" (3.188) |
| κηρὶ μελαίνῃ (3.454) | "the black death-fate" | "the black spirit of death" | the Iliad table’s κῆρα μέλαιναν (3.360), in the dative |
| τοῖσι δὲ καὶ μετέειπεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων (3.455, whole-line speech introduction) | "And among them spoke also the lord of men, Agamemnon:" | "And Agamemnon, lord of men, also spoke among them:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη); follows the Iliad’s τοῖσι δὲ καὶ μετέειπε βοὴν ἀγαθὸς Μενέλαος (3.96) |
| νίκη (νίκη … φαίνετ’, 3.457) | "victory" | "victory" | "triumph", "the win"; φαίνεται "appears" with the genitive, "belongs to" in `i` |
| ἔκδοτε (3.458–459) | "hand over" | "hand over" | "give up", "surrender"; kept apart from ἀποδοῦναι "give back" (3.285); ἐκδίδωμι "give out, hand over" |
| ἥ τε καὶ ἐσσομένοισι μετ’ ἀνθρώποισι πέληται (3.460 = 3.287) | "which shall be among men yet to come as well." | "one that will remain among men yet to come as well" | reused word for word from the shipped 3.287 (iliad-019), with the sentence frame changed around it |
| ὣς ἔφατ’ Ἀτρεΐδης, ἐπὶ δ’ ᾔνεον ἄλλοι Ἀχαιοί (3.461, whole line) | "So spoke Atreus’-son, and approved it the other Achaeans." | "So spoke the son of Atreus, and the rest of the Achaeans agreed." | "assented", "applauded" (reserved for ἐπῄνεον); the Odyssey table’s ὣς ἔφατ’ Εὐρύλοχος, ἐπὶ δ’ ᾔνεον ἄλλοι ἑταῖροι (12.294), with the name changed |
